scope: Conditional paper proof and optimization-design review only; no implemented C savings, actual allocator or deployment qualification.

reviewed_arguments.reason: At rotation k only old row k and evolving scratch x are read. No previously overwritten row is read by later k. Read-only candidate evaluation therefore has the same operand sequence as copied-factor or in-place insertion. Fixed scalar order, rounding, canonicalization, frozen input/configuration and reproducible row generation are indispensable. The complete real validation predicate set and generator scratch remain implementation obligations.

Prevalidation rejection leaves the complete old generation unchanged and the same input unconsumed. After overwrite begins there is no rollback factor; synchronized updating/quarantine must revoke current authority, and uncertain completion cannot be retried as ordinary unconsumed input. Qualified replay/checkpoint or information-losing public aged-support initialization is correctly required. This is consistent with A3/A4 and does not establish arbitrary-fault detection, durable resets or useful availability.

The streamed rows equal [U Dphi,U phi] rowwise, followed by original prior Jacobian/residual rows. Orthogonal insertion preserves the full augmented Gram matrix, including all cross terms and residual norm. For full-column-rank parameter Jacobian, R step=-c and R^T y=gq give joint GN step and local covariance; singularity remains explicitly unresolved. A general prior retains its full root and transformed derivatives. Damping is not evidence. Floating equality to dense BLAS and statistical coverage are not claimed.

Streaming retains old and staged response plus held sample and single QR row. Fit names root, features, emitted derivative, augmented row, distinct current/trial/step and scalar allowance. Trial rejection may recompute old linearization from immutable U. Query root and theta can survive the fit-to-query transition while fit-only buffers are released; query gradients can occupy the two in-place triangular-solve buffers. Five dynamic states and 5x16 sensitivities require 680 B. Streaming output and serialized phases are necessary; actual feature/response generators, helper frames, buffering and synchronization are explicitly excluded.

The comparisons use the source-bound old named ledger, not a universal lower bound or measured implementation. New peak remains partial. Generic prior adds 960 B; checkpoint/recovery redundancy is not hidden. SRAM feasibility and cadence feasibility remain open until all excluded costs and worst-case timing are measured and bound.

independent_checks.scope: Finite binary64 scalar algorithm witnesses with fixed random seed, including zero rows/roots and a nondiagonal full prior; no C allocation, fault injection, actual feature generator or lifetime qualification.

check_method: Independent Python/NumPy binary64 scalar insertion; sizes 1,3,17,34 and eight cases each, including zero root and zero row. Compared dry-run candidate bytes and unchanged input with copied-factor and in-place scalar paths. Separate 34-feature,16-parameter joint augmented QR included a random full triangular prior; compared Gram identity, least-squares step and two-query covariance to dense calculations. Source proof was not edited.
remaining_gate: Port exact row generator, all validations and scalar QR schedule in isolated C; prove/count all helper lifetimes.
Inject admission, mid-write, commit, duplicate, gap and reset faults with synchronized authority revocation; no ordinary retry after uncertain consumption.
Compare joint precision, gradient, cost, steps and transported covariance to dense reference with declared floating tolerances.
Bind compiled layout, full stack/library use, queues, ISR nesting, recovery storage, deadlines and CPU share before claiming ~10 KiB feasibility.
Independent optimization review and substantive-change re-review remain required.
